question: Map the likely lithium supply chain from Chile to a German battery manufacturer, identify ownership influence, and surface the strongest regulatory pressure points.

corpusDocuments.title: SQM ships lithium chemicals from Chile
corpusDocuments.text: SQM produces lithium carbonate in Chile from Salar de Atacama brine operations. The note says SQM ships lithium carbonate to Asian and European cathode supply chains through port logistics.

corpusDocuments.title: Tianqi exposure to SQM
corpusDocuments.text: An ownership brief says Tianqi Lithium holds a significant minority stake in SQM, creating board-level influence concerns even though SQM remains a Chilean operator.

corpusDocuments.title: German cathode and cell demand
corpusDocuments.text: A German battery manufacturing brief says local producers depend on imported lithium chemicals or processed cathode materials because domestic upstream refining remains limited.

corpusDocuments.title: Midstream concentration risk
corpusDocuments.text: A midstream risk memo states that lithium conversion capacity is concentrated in China, creating an intermediate choke point between Chilean raw or semi-processed output and European downstream manufacturing.

corpusDocuments.title: EU battery regulation pressure points
corpusDocuments.text: An EU regulatory summary highlights battery due diligence, carbon footprint disclosure, and traceability requirements as likely pressure points for imported battery materials entering Germany.

corpusDocuments.title: Open gap on exact converter identity
corpusDocuments.text: A gap note says the supplied corpus does not identify a specific Chinese or European converter handling the Chilean lithium before it reaches Germany.
